exactSourceAndSingleSubmission: Workflow jobs require repository alexj11324/Mikka and refs/heads/main; expected-deployment-sha must be a 40-hex SHA equal to GITHUB_SHA before credentials.

The legacy ops dispatcher separately checks current main ref and the official /mikka/api/version served build before the dispatch POST. Acceptance driver pins the served build before login, before each case, before paid submission and again at completion; browser actor checks source context and served version before login and immediately before submit.

Runner browser additionally requires execute + browser-submit + exactly one case, a real workflow_dispatch/main context and exact expected SHA. Chromium uses a clean independent context; no copied cookie, storageState, fabricated trace/session or direct task-submission API.

Driver derives a deterministic temporary Profile per deployment/model and rejects a previous fixture. The actor records one submit click before click and never retries after uncertainty. The driver validates one actual new human message and exact task/Profile/identity/model/native-stage/Artifact/acceptance receipts.

Per-case default deadline is 480000 ms; permitted range 60000..600000. Flow v2 expects distinct execute + review, legacy adds verify. Attempt overrun stops on observation; no atomic spend fence or hard-dollar guarantee is claimed.
Browser progress comment explicitly says the runner submits automatically and manual submission must not duplicate it.
recoveryAndCleanup: CLI wires onRecoveryCheckpoint to writeRecoveryJournal. Journal is a complete safe metadata snapshot: private wx 0600 temporary file, file fsync, rename to recovery.json, then directory fsync.

Journal checkpoints record mutation intent before fallback/Profile/model writes and acknowledged version/digest or temporarySelection receipt after success. A failed checkpoint blocks new work and marks final result blocked, while already-required cleanup remains allowed.
Full private Profile definitions remain in RAM. Journal retains scope IDs, old enabled/version/digest and exact model identity/restoration receipt, not prompt/account contents.

Settings restoration checks owner-wide visible idle state and existing acknowledged values. Profile restore uses current version/digest and CAS; implicit model restoration uses returned binding/revision. Explicit composer and fallback booleans have optimistic checks, not an atomic ABA-proof guarantee.

Cleanup only cancels owned unfinished Factory work and active threads, then ends every owned native run's machine including success cases. Ended requires exact HTTP 200 run/state receipt; 404 requires fresh terminal own run plus explicit null machine. A state read alone is not termination proof.
Temporary Profile archive and original composer restoration occur only when owned work is quiet; concurrent edits are preserved. Incomplete cleanup stops later cases and makes status blocked.

Browser first closes its page to prevent pending UI clicks, signs out using retained context, reads anonymous session, then closes context/browser with its own bounded cleanup deadline. Helper waits for both owned lifecycles.

Driver session is signed out in finally. A process kill that prevents finally cannot guarantee automatic restoration; inspect retained recovery.json and receipts before any new case. The 5f workflow now uploads report.json, recovery.json and browser-actor.receipt.json under always().
